citations.excerpt: List two suitable reliability metrices for the system. [2 marks]
Are (for our purposes) about software reliability, not hardware reliability. Must be based on a kind of measurement that actually makes sense for the particular system.

recall.a: MTTF/MTBF (mean time to/between failures), Availability (uptime fraction), POFOD (probability of failure on demand), ROCOF (failure rate). Choose the metric that fits the usage pattern: POFOD for on-demand checks, availability for continuous monitoring.
recall.q: Name the four reliability metrics and the rule for choosing between them.

sections.heading: Introduction
paras: Reliability is, basically, the probability the software does its job when asked — but 'when asked' differs by system, so the unit teaches four metrics and insists you choose the one that fits. The 2022 patient monitor and 2019 restaurant questions both punish metric-mismatch: POFOD for a continuous display is as wrong as availability for a rare on-demand check.

sections.heading: The four metrics
paras: The worksheet's three commandments: reliability here means software reliability (not hardware); the metric must make sense for the particular system (hint aimed at POFOD-vs-availability traps); and the requirement states an acceptable failure level for a stated failure class — never perfection, always specific. Systems fail in some ways and not others, and some failures matter more: say which failures you mean.

sections.heading: Worked answers
paras: 2022 Q3.4(b) metrics for the patient monitor: availability ('the display function shall be available at least 99.9% of monitoring time') and ROCOF or MTTF for the sensing pipeline — both fit continuous operation. Q3.4(c) requirement: 'The system shall lose no more than 1 minute of displayed vital-sign data per 24 hours of continuous operation, with any sensor failure annunciated within 5 seconds.' Bound, workload, failure class, detection — every validity property satisfied.

2019 restaurant hint ('not all metrics make sense here'): payment processing is on-demand (POFOD fits), while the kitchen display during service hours is continuous (availability fits). Naming the mismatch explicitly is what the 3 marks buy.

summary: Reliability is failure behaviour quantified: MTTF/MTBF, availability, POFOD, ROCOF — chosen to fit the usage pattern, bounded short of perfection, scoped to a failure class.
